title: Reuse a passed CI result for the same governed fingerprint
summary: Make the 'fmt, clippy, tests' job compute the governed-content fingerprint and look it up in CI's own actions/cache. If a passing entry exists it reports that result and skips setup and the build. Otherwise it runs the full suite and saves a pass on success. Athena land (gh.rs) pushes the verified candidate to a ref at verification start so CI has a passing result before landing. Audience: Athena maintainers who wait on landing.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria require tests showing reuse, rerun and failure behavior, not just that files exist.
Tests in xtask and gh.rs; cargo test and clippy are clean.
decisions.md cites the measured 15.4 minute median and labels the 'after' as pending if it is not measured.
The reuse rule is enforced in code and workflow, with tests.
One focused change limited to the files listed.
The fix targets the repeated full run on an identical governed fingerprint.
A missing or failed cache result never passes.
Comments and docs are written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: shorten landing by skipping the repeated full CI run when governed content is unchanged. Audience: Athena maintainers and the verifier.
The fingerprint function is reused from athena-gate/athena-git, not reimplemented. xtask may call the athena binary or the crate; the producer picks whichever keeps the fingerprint single-sourced.
CI's cache is actions/cache keyed on the fingerprint, holding a small pass marker. The job name stays unchanged, and skipped steps still make the job succeed.
The 'after' landing times cannot be measured inside this change. The decisions entry records 'before' and a clearly marked pending 'after', to be filled by a later landing.

Pushing early uses a ref or branch that triggers the push event on CI, so a passing cache entry exists before the PR commit lands. Cache entries made on a non-default ref may not be visible to other refs, so the producer must check GitHub's cache scoping. Saving from the default-branch ref or the PR base may be needed.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new xtask test (run: cargo test -p xtask) shows that after a passing result is stored for a fingerprint, a change touching only records/ or owner paths yields the same fingerprint and reuses the result, and a change to a governed file yields a different fingerprint and runs the full job.
A test (run: cargo test -p xtask) shows that a missing, failed, malformed or unreadable cached result never lets the job pass. It runs the full checks.

ci.yml keeps the job name 'fmt, clippy, tests'. It keys the cache only on the governed fingerprint. It saves an entry only after the full run passes. It reads no Athena records. The save step is restricted so unreviewed pull requests cannot poison the entry (or the trust model is stated in a comment).

A test in gh.rs (run: cargo test -p athena-core) shows that athena land, when verification starts, pushes the candidate for CI through the Host seam, and that a push failure does not fail verification. Landing still waits on the required check.

docs/decisions.md has a dated entry with the measured landing time before (median 15.4 minutes over 33 jobs, 2026-10-23 to 2026-10-25), the mechanism and the rejected alternatives. It has an 'after' section that is filled only from landings actually run after the change, or is labeled pending with no invented numbers.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the change. cargo test, cargo clippy -D warnings and cargo fmt --check pass.

out_of_scope: Changing the other CI jobs (history, attribution, pr-head)
Changing the ruleset, athena.toml or defaults.toml
Trusting Athena's records as evidence of a CI pass
Fixing unrelated slowness in the build or tests
departures: This touches the workflow, xtask and the landing code, with tests for each, so cost and time are higher than the reference. The cache-scoping and trust questions raise the chance that verification fails.
